title: "Hallucination"
description: "An AI-generated claim or output that is unsupported, fabricated, or inconsistent with available evidence."
term: "Hallucination"
letter: "H"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

An AI hallucination is an output that sounds plausible but is false,
unsupported, or inconsistent with the information available to the
system.

## Technical explanation

The term is commonly used for language-model outputs that contain
fabricated facts, citations, or details. The cause may involve
uncertainty, missing context, training-data patterns, decoding, or
application design. Definitions and evaluation criteria vary by task.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Unsupported outputs can mislead users and cause harm, especially in
high-impact contexts. Systems need task-specific evaluations,
appropriate sourcing, uncertainty handling, and human review where
necessary.

## How it works

A generative model produces outputs based on learned patterns and
available context. It may generate a likely continuation even when it
lacks reliable evidence. Retrieval, tools, constrained output formats,
and verification can reduce some errors but do not eliminate them.

## Practical example

A question-answering system may invent a page number for a real report.
Checking citations against the source document can detect this error.

## Common misconceptions

- Hallucination is not limited to made-up names; wrong details and
  unsupported inferences also matter.
- Retrieval-augmented generation does not eliminate hallucinations.
- A confident tone is not evidence that an answer is correct.
